The company has a clear AI strategy focusing on data sovereignty and ethical AI usage.<SEP>Ouest-France is a media organization that demands data sovereignty and internal AI vision compliance in document processing.<SEP>Ouest-France is a prominent French media organization engaged in print media and digital platforms, and recognized as a leading daily newspaper in France.<SEP>Ouest-France is an organization where the author of the document interned, working on developing a machine learning pipeline for automated article extraction from historical newspaper archives.

The SIPA Ouest-France group

data.entity_name: Machine Learning Pipeline for Automated Extraction of Articles
data.content:
Machine Learning Pipeline for Automated Extraction of Articles
A project developed during Valentin Peron's internship to automate the extraction of articles from newspaper archives using a custom pipeline that operates locally within the Ouest-France infrastructure.

Ouest-Éclair
Ouest-Éclair is the former name of the newspaper now known as Ouest-France, covering the period from 1899 to 2000.<SEP>Ouest-Éclair is the former title of Ouest-France, changed after World War II, and involved in the article extraction project.

Baye-Lahad Mbacke
Baye-Lahad Mbacke is a member of the SIRAI team at Ouest-France, contributing to Valentin Peron's internship project.

Thomas Girault
Thomas Girault is a member of the SIRAI team at Ouest-France, contributing to Valentin Peron's internship project.

Ibrahima Ba
Ibrahima Ba is a member of the SIRAI team at Ouest-France, contributing to Valentin Peron's internship project.

Melvin Leveque
Melvin Leveque is a member of the SIRAI team at Ouest-France, contributing to Valentin Peron's internship project.

Cédric Jezequel
Cédric Jezequel is a member of the SIRAI team at Ouest-France, contributing to Valentin Peron's internship project.

Cédric Moreau
Cédric Moreau is a member of the SIRAI team at Ouest-France, contributing to Valentin Peron's internship project.

Fabrice Bazard
Fabrice Bazard is the General Director at Ouest-France, playing a key leadership role within the organization.

Christophe Duprat
Christophe Duprat is the Director of Information Systems at Ouest-France, responsible for managing the organization's information systems.

10 Rue du Breil, Chantepie
The headquarters of Ouest-France is located at 10 Rue du Breil, Chantepie, where the internship mentioned in the text took place.

War in Ukraine
The War in Ukraine is mentioned as part of the challenging global context impacting Ouest-France's financial performance.

SIRAI team
The SIRAI team is part of Ouest-France, focusing on exploring and developing AI-based solutions, including the Data Science pole.

Data Science pole
The Data Science pole is a division within the SIRAI team responsible for R&D, building AI models, and responding to departmental requests within Ouest-France.

Products and Services pole
The Products and Services pole manages the 'Valorisation' platform, ensuring AI models from the Data Science team are integrated and deployed into production.

AI Charter
Ouest-France has an internal AI Charter outlining ethical and responsible AI use, emphasizing data sovereignty, editorial independence, and data protection.

Internship
An Internship serves as the context during which various strategies for document layout detection and article segmentation are explored and tested.<SEP>The Internship refers to the period during which the pipeline architecture was developed, involving exploratory research and iterative improvements.<SEP>The Internship took place at Ouest-France, involving integration into the SIRAI team and a project focused on indexing historical newspaper pages.<SEP>This was an internship where the author worked on developing a machine learning pipeline for extracting articles from historical newspaper archives.

World War II
World War II is referenced in the context of Ouest-Éclair changing its name to Ouest-France after being liberated during the war.

RAG (Retrieval Augmented Generation)
RAG is a technology mentioned in the context of using newspaper articles as a source for a chatbot to answer questions regarding historical data.

Newspaper indexing pipeline
The newspaper indexing pipeline was developed to extract articles from high resolution scans of historical newspaper pages from Ouest-France and Ouest-Éclair.

Historical newspaper pages
Refers to the content of newspaper pages from Ouest-France and Ouest-Éclair covering the period 1899 to 2000, subject to the article extraction project.

Tesseract
Tesseract is a traditional OCR engine that faced challenges in processing complex historical newspaper layouts.<SEP>Tesseract is a traditional OCR engine that performed poorly on historical documents due to text and layout complexities.

EasyOCR
EasyOCR is a traditional OCR engine that struggled with inconsistent formatting and degraded text in historical documents.<SEP>EasyOCR is a traditional OCR engine that, like Tesseract, struggled with the complex layouts of historical newspapers, prompting exploration of more advanced methods.

Vision Language Models (VLMs)
Vision Language Models are advanced OCR solutions combining natural language understanding with image analysis for reconstructing complex and damaged text.

Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct
Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct is an open-source VLM capable of interpreting complex visual content and spotting damaged or incomplete text.

vLLM
vLLM is a fast and scalable library used for LLM and VLM inference, enhancing the performance of OCR applications.

Indexing Pipeline
The Indexing Pipeline is a modular system developed to handle large-scale, high-resolution document analysis, addressing issues like layout detection, text extraction, and article segmentation.

Pipeline Architecture
Pipeline Architecture refers to the systematic design and structure of the indexing pipeline, incorporating layout detection, text extraction, and article segmentation.

Traditional OCR Tools
Traditional OCR Tools describes conventional optical character recognition engines like Tesseract and EasyOCR, used for converting images to text.

High Resolution Newspaper Pages
High Resolution Newspaper Pages are historical documents with complex layouts and formats, posing a challenge for traditional OCR technology.

Article Segmentation
Article Segmentation is a step in the indexing pipeline where extracted text blocks are grouped into meaningful articles.<SEP>Article Segmentation is the process of grouping detected text blocks into meaningful articles, which is a complex task due to diverse newspaper layouts and content types.<SEP>Article Segmentation refers to the process of dividing a document into discrete articles, which remains a significant challenge requiring further research and experimentation.

Text Extraction (OCR)
Text Extraction (OCR) is a crucial process in the indexing pipeline, focused on converting detected blocks into text format.

Layout Detection
Layout Detection is a process in the pipeline that identifies and classifies different blocks within newspaper pages.

VLM based OCR
VLM based OCR refers to vision-language models used to provide state-of-the-art results in text recognition for old, damaged, and multicolumn newspaper text.

GPU
GPU (Graphics Processing Unit) is used to handle large computational tasks during model processing, such as in LLM-based grouping strategies.<SEP>The GPU, or Graphics Processing Unit, experienced issues with VRAM capacity when processing entire newspaper pages, prompting a redesign of the system pipeline.

YOLO11-Document-Layout-Analysis
YOLO11-Document-Layout-Analysis is a model based on the YOLO11 architecture, adapted for document layout recognition to detect classes such as caption, footnote, and table.

DocLayNet
DocLayNet is a dataset known in document layout recognition, used for adapting YOLO11-Document-Layout-Analysis for detecting different document structures.

internship presentation
An internship presentation inspired the development of logic-based rules for improving layout detection based on position, size, and proximity of bounding boxes.

historical document analysis
Historical document analysis is the field focused on processing and interpreting old documents, relevant to the challenges of multicolumn and degraded newspaper layouts.

OCR engine
The OCR engine is used to process isolated text regions from newspaper pages after layout detection, allowing for successful text recognition without exceeding memory limits.

Hugging Face
Hugging Face is a platform offering various models, including those for layout detection, although initially the available models did not perform well on historical newspapers.

YOLO11
YOLO11 is part of an ensemble approach for enhanced layout detection across varied newspaper formats.<SEP>YOLO11, or 'You Only Look Once', is a model architecture originally created for object recognition and adapted for document layout analysis.

rules-based post-processing
Rules-based post-processing refers to the logic-based rules developed to refine layout detection outputs by merging, filtering, and reducing noise among detected regions.

bounding boxes
Bounding boxes are regions identified by the layout detection model to segment various document elements, such as text and images, which require further processing for accuracy.

ensemble approach
The ensemble approach involves combining multiple layout detection methods to enhance accuracy and robustness when parsing diverse historical newspaper formats.

PaddleOCR
PaddleOCR is the organization that developed the PP-DocLayout-L, a document layout detection model designed for complex document structures and high-resolution images.

PP-DocLayout-L
PP-DocLayout-L is a document layout detection model developed by PaddleOCR, specifically designed for complex document structures and high-resolution images.<SEP>PP-DocLayout-L is part of an ensemble approach that improved robustness in layout detection for newspapers of different formats.

YOLO-based model
The YOLO-based model is a fast layout detection model that often produces overlapping or redundant bounding boxes, but is useful for detecting smaller or irregular blocks in documents.

Ensemble Approach
Ensemble Approach refers to the method of combining multiple models to leverage each model's strengths and compensate for individual weaknesses, resulting in more robust and accurate predictions.

HDBSCAN
HDBSCAN is a density-based clustering algorithm used to detect clusters of semantically similar blocks in the context of article segmentation.

Large Language Models (LLMs)
Large Language Models (LLMs) are used in this context to predict which text blocks should be grouped together based on their content and spatial information.

Vision-Language Model (VLM)
Vision-Language Model (VLM) is used to pre-extract article titles to guide the grouping process in article segmentation.<SEP>Vision-Language Model (VLM) refers to a type of model used to pre-extract article titles, aimed at improving the grouping process of newspaper articles.

Embedding Cosine Similarity Matrix
Embedding Cosine Similarity Matrix is used to identify blocks with related content by representing each text block as a vector capturing its meaning.

Rule-based post-processing
Rule-based post-processing is a method used to improve results for a specific subset of pages in document layout detection, though it lacks robustness to handle the full diversity of an archive.

Hybrid system
The Hybrid system refers to the combination of PP-DocLayout-L and YOLO-based models in a layout detection approach, aiming to harness the strengths of both for improved accuracy.

Semantic embeddings
Semantic embeddings are used to represent each text block as a vector capturing its meaning, aiming to identify blocks with related content during article segmentation.

Bounding boxes
Bounding boxes are used in layout detection models to identify and highlight specific areas or blocks within a document.

Newspaper pages from 1899 to the 1990s
This category represents the dataset of newspaper pages being analyzed for layout detection, highlighting the historical and diverse nature of the documents.

Data science
Data science is the field that involves using techniques like ensembling to solve complex challenges such as document layout detection and text clustering.

Complex document structures
Complex document structures refer to the intricate and varied formatting found in documents, posing challenges for precise layout detection.

High-resolution images
High-resolution images are used in conjunction with document layout models to ensure accuracy and detail in detection processes.

Text blocks
Text blocks are sections of text within a document layout that are detected and grouped during the processing pipeline.

Clustering algorithms
Clustering algorithms group similar data points together based on specific criteria, such as semantic similarity in text blocks.

Degraded regions of documents
Degraded regions of documents are areas where the text or images have been damaged, complicating layout detection.

LayoutLM
LayoutLM is a document layout analysis model designed to provide structural awareness and facilitate better article segmentation compared to general-purpose models.

Graph Neural Networks (GNNs)
Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) are described as a promising option for representing detected blocks as nodes in a graph to reconstruct full articles.

Qwen 2.5 VL (7B)
Qwen 2.5 VL (7B) is a Vision Language Model used as part of an advanced method deployed to improve newspaper article extraction.

Group Position Embedding (GPE)
Group Position Embedding (GPE) is a technique designed to enhance layout understanding in machine learning models without architectural changes.

Intern
The intern is the person who worked on developing the machine learning pipeline for Ouest-France during their internship.

Spatial Information
Spatial Information is a crucial component that plays a role in defining what constitutes an article, indicating the importance of layout and position.

Semantic Similarity
Semantic Similarity is described as insufficient alone in grouping diverse content types in newspaper pages, highlighting the need for hybrid methods.

Machine Learning Pipeline
Machine Learning Pipeline refers to the system being developed to automate the extraction of articles from historical newspapers at Ouest-France.

OCR Engines
OCR Engines refers to Optical Character Recognition engines like Tesseract and EasyOCR, which faced challenges with historical newspaper layouts.

Multicolumn Documents
Multicolumn Documents are high-resolution newspaper formats with varied and complex layouts, presenting challenges for OCR and layout analysis.
